title: When the Harbor Falls
premise: In 1847, in the fog-bound port town of Grayharbor, Mirabel Blackwood is summoned from his master's workshop to repair the observatory's failing master clock—the very clock whose chimes the army uses to synchronize its requisitions. When soldiers seize the town and confiscate the harbor ledger holding every debt, name, and inheritance, Mirabel realizes the clock's hidden escapement was built by his grandfather to encode those names, and the army wants it silenced. Racing to finish the repair before the workshop is demolished, he must choose between restoring the clock to army time or setting it to ring out the true ledger, exposing the colonel who forged his own inheritance from Grayharbor's seized fortunes. In the end, the clock strikes the names at dawn, the town rises, and Mirabel inherits not the workshop but the obligation to keep time honestly.
about_author: Xanthe Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing port-town ledgers and probate records along the northern coast. Their fiction explores what ordinary tradespeople carry when history arrives with paperwork and guns.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV, catalogs the workshop's tools as his dying master, Odell, sends him to the observatory with a single instruction: listen before you touch. Mirabel measures the world in what can be carried. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional pride.

chapters.title: A summons in Fog
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Climbing to the observatory, he meets the keeper's daughter, Sable Voss, who warns him the master clock hasn't struck true in a year—deliberately, she suspects. He finds a hidden second escapement inside the case. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: What the Escapement Keeps
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He deciphers the escapement's odd teeth and realizes they encode numbers—debt tallies, dates, initials. Odell's warning echoes: listen before you touch. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into fear of what it means.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Punctual Men
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Grayharbor wakes to red-coated soldiers at every pier. Colonel Ashgrave announces requisition 'for the war effort' and demands the harbor ledger. Sable watches her father hand it over with shaking hands. Emotional beat: helplessness as order becomes occupation.

chapters.title: Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The army seizes the workshop district; Odell's ledger of apprentices, debts, and inheritances is confiscated with everything else. Mirabel hides the escapement drawings in his coat lining. Emotional beat: the moment invisibility dies.

chapters.title: Time Belongs to the Crown Now
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV. The colonel orders the observatory clock converted to army time and the workshop slated for demolition in three weeks. He suspects the clock holds more than gears—his own grandfather's name may be in it. Emotional beat: cold ambition masking fear.

chapters.title: Listening Before Touching
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Allowed to work under guard, Mirabel studies the clock without repairing it, buying time. Sable smuggles him Odell's old letters. Emotional beat: patience as quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: The Letters of Odell Blackwood
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The letters reveal his grandfather built the escapement to preserve the town's true ledger when the harbor company began erasing debts. Mirabel understands his summons was inheritance, not accident. Emotional beat: grief transforming into purpose.

chapters.title: A Town Measured in Debts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She gathers whispers from dockworkers whose names were struck from the ledger—families who lost boats, houses, children's inheritances to Ashgrave's grandfather. Emotional beat: shared anger finding a shape.

chapters.title: Three Weeks on the Dial
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Demolition is moved up to ten days. He begins the repair in earnest, but a soldier sergeant, Brann, watches too closely and asks the wrong questions. Emotional beat: the clock ticking against him literally.

chapters.title: The Sergeant Who Counts
chapters.summary: Brann's POV. A conscripted accountant-soldier, Brann notices the escapement's teeth don't match any regulation design and quietly copies them, torn between duty and the memory of his own father's seized farm. Emotional beat: complicity cracking.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Soldiers loot the workshop; Mirabel saves only his grandfather's tools and the escapement drawings, measuring his life into one satchel. Odell dies that night. Emotional beat: loss stripped to essentials, resolve hardened.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV. He burns the harbor ledger's pages bearing his family's forged claims, believing the clock's secret dies with the paper. He orders Mirabel to finish by Friday or hang. Emotional beat: power devouring its own proof.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She trades her father's observatory keys to Brann in exchange for the confiscated ledger's surviving index, gambling everything on a clockmaker she's known two weeks. Emotional beat: trust as an act of courage.

chapters.title: Cutting a New Tooth
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Working by candlelight in the half-demolished workshop, Mirabel recuts the escapement to ring the names—the true ledger—in chimes the whole harbor can read. Emotional beat: craft as resistance, terror and exaltation entwined.

chapters.title: Brann's Choice
chapters.summary: Brann's POV. Ordered to arrest Mirabel for tampering, Brann instead delivers the index pages to the observatory and deserts. Emotional beat: a man choosing justice outside the law at the cost of everything he was.

chapters.title: The Night Before Friday
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Assembly complete but untested, the clock waits. Sable and Mirabel keep vigil among the gears; she asks what he'll do if no one listens. He answers: the clock will listen for them. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: Dawn of the Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climactic. At dawn the master clock strikes not the hour but the sequence—names, debts, dates—rolling over the occupied harbor. Dockworkers, fishermen, and soldiers' own families pour into the streets. Ashgrave orders the clock shot down. Emotional beat: the town hearing itself for the first time in a generation.

chapters.title: What the Bell Cannot Break
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Soldiers fire on the observatory; Brann shields the escapement with his body and is wounded. The crowd, armed with hammers and hooks, surrounds the square. Ashgrave's own men hesitate, hearing their fathers' names in the bells. Emotional beat: courage multiplying faster than fear.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV, climax. Confronted in the clock room by Mirabel, Sable, and the crowd, Ashgrave claims the law is his. Mirabel answers that the clock has kept better accounts than any court. Ashgrave's own sergeant arrests him for forgery and theft of inheritances. Emotional beat: power collapsing under its own ledger.

chapters.title: Setting the Town's Time
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Weeks later, the harbor ledger is rebuilt from the escapement's record; debts are restored, inheritances returned. Mirabel declines the magistrate's offer of office, choosing instead to reopen the workshop. Emotional beat: justice as ongoing work, not a verdict.

chapters.title: The Hands He Winds
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, resolution. Mirabel takes Sable as partner, trains Brann—now a free man—as an apprentice, and hangs Odell's portrait above the bench. Each dawn he winds the master clock himself, listening before he touches. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled; time kept honestly at last.
